```{r}
#| include: false
# Only cheap objects here. The landing page must not pull in the model, or
# every visit to the front door pays for a render of the whole analysis.
rc  <- readRDS(here::here("data", "reception_cohort.rds"))
oi  <- readRDS(here::here("data", "open_inputs.rds"))

y7_peak   <- max(rc$secondary_city$y7_offers)
y7_peak_y <- rc$secondary_city$year[which.max(rc$secondary_city$y7_offers)]
y7_end    <- rc$projection$central[which.max(rc$projection$entry_year)]
y7_end_y  <- max(rc$projection$entry_year)
y7_drop   <- round((y7_peak - y7_end) / 10) * 10
# Peacehaven sits in East Sussex and is in the model only because it takes
# children from the east of the city, so it is not one of Brighton & Hove's
# own secondaries.
n_city <- sum(oi$schools$catchment != "Peacehaven" | is.na(oi$schools$catchment))
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",")
```

[A strategic view]{.hero-label}

# Brighton & Hove's secondary school system

In ten years this city has to run a school system for roughly
`r fmt(y7_drop)` fewer children a year than it has now. This site is an
attempt to say — from published data, in the open — what that actually
means, and what the options are.
:::
:::

::: {.landing-wrap}

::: {.landing-lede}
Brighton & Hove has ten secondary schools, a cohort that peaked in
`r y7_peak_y` and is falling, and a sequence of admissions decisions each
argued about on its own. What has been missing is an account of how the
whole system behaves: where the children are, how families choose, what
each policy does to every other school, and which combinations leave the
city with a viable set of schools in 2035.

That account is below, together with a simulator you can put your own
scenarios through. **Everything here is built from published data.** No
pupil records are used anywhere.
:::

::: {.landing-note}
**On the data.** Everything on this site is built from published sources:
DfE performance tables and the statistics API, the council's own
allocation factsheets going back to 2010, the 2021 Census, OpenStreetMap
and the real bus timetable, and one Freedom of Information request. The
code is [open on GitHub](https://github.com/adamdennett/bh-school-system).
No pupil-level data is used anywhere.
:::
